summary: The ladder starts with headline year-to-date growth, then shows that new stores and an early-year ramp drive most of it while the established stores slow down after summer as they lose customers and visits. It ends by sizing the levers: winning back lost customers, lifting baskets and growing the new stores.

narration.text: Gross revenue for January to October reached $1.91M, up 178.9% on the $685.4K earned in the same months last year.
Brooklyn grew fastest among the stores with a full prior year, with revenue of $1.03M against $222.0K last year, up 365.6%, while Philadelphia reached $673.6K, up 45.4%.
Chicago and San Francisco opened in July, so they have no prior year to compare, and they added $115.9K and $88.1K.
Month by month, growth against last year has slowed from 572.9% in January to 106.2% in October, though monthly revenue itself has held between $158.1K and $240.4K.

The new stores are propping up the recent total, because Brooklyn fell from $115.8K in July to $84.7K in October and Philadelphia from $71.0K to $55.3K, while Chicago and San Francisco rose to $36.5K and $32.0K.

In the established stores the number of customers is flat, with Brooklyn at 699 in September and Philadelphia at 448, so the slowdown comes from fewer visits per customer, which fell in Brooklyn from 15.6 orders in July to 12.8 in September and in Philadelphia from 14.0 to 11.4.
Average order value has barely moved, at $10.32 in Brooklyn and $11.42 in Philadelphia in October, so spending per visit is not the problem.

The first lever is winning back what the established stores have lost since July, which the next chart sizes: Brooklyn's revenue is down $31.1K and 150 customers, and Philadelphia's is down $15.7K and 88 customers.
Focus on bringing lapsed customers back in Brooklyn and Philadelphia, since their October customer counts of 548 and 360 are well below the 699 and 448 they had in September.
Test lifting average order at the stores below the best basket, because the scorecard shows Brooklyn at $10.32 and Chicago at $10.55 against Philadelphia at $11.42.
Ramp Chicago and San Francisco towards established-store frequency, as their 13.5 and 12.7 orders per customer trail Brooklyn's 15.0.

digests.summary: Gross revenue for January to October was $1.91M, up 178.9% from $685.4K a year earlier, led by Brooklyn at 365.6% and Philadelphia at 45.4%, with Chicago and San Francisco opened in July. Monthly growth against last year has slowed from 572.9% in January to 106.2% in October.

digests.question: Why is growth slowing?
digests.headline: fewer visits per customer
digests.summary: Gross revenue for January to October was $1.91M, up 178.9% from $685.4K a year earlier, led by Brooklyn at 365.6%, but growth against last year has slowed to 106.2% in October. Established stores are shrinking because customers make fewer visits, not because they spend less per order, and the new Chicago and San Francisco stores are covering the gap.

digests.question: What should we do?
digests.headline: win back visits
digests.summary: Gross revenue for January to October was $1.91M, up 178.9%, but growth has slowed to 106.2% in October because established stores see fewer visits per customer while new stores cover the gap. The levers are winning back lapsed customers in Brooklyn and Philadelphia, lifting basket where it trails, and ramping Chicago and San Francisco frequency.
